plan: This is a second-price auction (like Vickrey auction) where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher than value risks winning at a loss; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid exactly my value of $32.

In a second-price auction, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. This ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest competing bid, and my profit is maximized without risk of overpaying, since I only pay the second-highest bid regardless of how high my own bid is. Bidding above value risks negative profit if I win at a price above my value; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $6, bidding $6 is optimal.

This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I bid exactly my value ($17), I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and I pay that second-highest bid (always less than my value), guaranteeing non-negative profit. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if I win; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, my optimal bid is simply $17.
